rationale: The first reply was reasonable: it said the bulb is user-replaceable and pointed to an E14 300°C lamp, though it stayed vague on wattage. The second reply reversed this, wrongly claiming the lamp is in a sealed unit that needs disassembly and sending the customer to an engineer. This contradicts the first reply and ignores the customer's stated isolation and cooling plan. The customer got no cover-removal steps and no clear bulb spec, and the unnecessary escalation was unhelpful. The reply also said the model was not found in the parts catalogue, which has no bearing on a simple bulb swap.
